glossary.AST: Aspartate aminotransferase, a liver enzyme released when liver cells are damaged.
glossary.Incubation: Time from catching an infection to developing symptoms.
glossary.Self-limiting: Gets better on its own without specific treatment.
glossary.Co-infection: Being infected with two viruses at the same time.
glossary.Infectivity: How easily an infected person passes the virus on.
glossary.Jaundice: Yellowing of the skin and eyes from raised bilirubin in the blood.
glossary.RUQ: Right upper quadrant of the abdomen, where the liver sits.
glossary.Trimester: One of the three roughly three-month stages of pregnancy.
glossary.Fulminant hepatic failure: Sudden, severe liver failure with encephalopathy in someone without previous liver disease.
glossary.Cirrhosis: Irreversible scarring of the liver with regenerating nodules, replacing normal tissue.
glossary.HIV: Human immunodeficiency virus, which weakens immunity and can blunt vaccine responses.
glossary.Chronic liver disease: Long-term liver damage lasting over six months, often leading to cirrhosis.
glossary.Serology: Blood tests for antibodies or antigens to a pathogen.
glossary.Viral hepatitis screen: Panel of blood tests for hepatitis A to E antibodies, antigens and viral genetic material.
glossary.HCV RNA: The genetic material of hepatitis C; detecting it means active infection.
glossary.Anti-HAV IgM: Antibody showing recent hepatitis A infection.
glossary.Anti-HEV IgM: Antibody showing recent hepatitis E infection.
glossary.Synthetic liver function: The liver's ability to make proteins such as albumin and clotting factors.
glossary.Albumin: Main blood protein made by the liver; low in poor synthetic function.
glossary.FBC: Full blood count: haemoglobin, white cells and platelets.
glossary.U&Es: Urea and electrolytes: blood tests of kidney function.
glossary.Viral load: Amount of virus in the blood.
glossary.Supportive care: Treatment of symptoms and complications while the body clears the infection.
glossary.Contact screening: Testing people who have been in close contact with an infected person.
glossary.Non-enveloped: A virus with no outer lipid coat, so it survives in the gut and the environment.
glossary.Chronic carriage: Long-term persistence of a virus in the body.
glossary.Immunosuppressed: Having a weakened immune system from disease or drugs.
glossary.Double-stranded DNA: DNA made of two paired strands, which HBV can insert into host DNA.
glossary.Immune-mediated: Caused by the body's own immune response rather than the virus directly.
glossary.Cytopathic: Directly damaging or killing the cells a virus infects.
glossary.Mutation rate: How often errors arise when a virus copies its genome.
glossary.Immune clearance: The immune system removing an infection from the body.
glossary.NS3/4A protease: Hepatitis C enzyme that cuts viral proteins; blocked by some DAAs.
glossary.NS5A: Hepatitis C protein needed for replication; targeted by velpatasvir and ledipasvir.
glossary.NS5B polymerase: Hepatitis C enzyme that copies viral RNA; blocked by sofosbuvir.
glossary.Defective virus: A virus that cannot replicate or form particles without help from another virus.
glossary.Envelope: Outer lipid coat of a virus.
glossary.Genome integration: A virus inserting its genetic material into the host cell's DNA.
